title: File:Datong Ancient City Wall 01.jpg

Categories.value: Files with coordinates missing SDC location of creation|Flickr images reviewed by FlickreviewR 2|Datong City Wall (reconstruction)

ImageDescription.value: The Datong Ancient City Wall in Datong, Shanxi, China, originally built in 421 during the Northern Wei Dynasty, was reinforced in 1372 during the Ming Dynasty by General Xu Da. Standing 14 meters high with a perimeter of 7.24 kilometers, it features four main gates—Heyang, Yongtai, Qingyuan, and Wuding—along with watchtowers, barbicans, and a moat, forming a robust military defense system. Restored between 2008 and 2010, the wall showcases ancient Chinese architectural prowess and offers panoramic views of the city, blending historical significance with cultural heritage.

title: File:凤凰古城 2024-06-22 12.jpg

Categories.value: Files with coordinates missing SDC location of creation|Flickr images reviewed by FlickreviewR 2|Photographs by Xiquinho Silva|Fenghuang Ancient Town

ImageDescription.value:
Fenghuang Ancient City, also known as Phoenix Ancient Town, is a historical gem located in the Hunan province of China. This well-preserved town is celebrated for its unique stilted houses, vibrant cultural tapestry woven by the Miao and Tujia ethnic minorities, and the picturesque Tuojiang River that meanders through it. 
Visitors to Fenghuang can explore the narrow alleys lined with traditional wooden houses, witness the daily life of locals along the riverbanks, and immerse themselves in a place where history and culture have remained largely intact through the centuries.
